name: checkbox
purpose: Binary selection control. Supports a single boolean (`binary: true`) and array-based multi-select (adds or removes its `value` in the `modelValue` array) (used by `MultiSelect` and `DataTable` to drive bulk selection). The new `indeterminate` prop renders a third visual state (horizontal bar) and sets the native `indeterminate` property, which exposes the mixed state — used by parents that own a partial-selection summary (e.g. "select all" rows where some children are selected). Aligned with Figma frame `2027:7311`.
useWhen: A bare boolean control whose label lives outside it: a table row-selection cell, an option row in a list, a settings matrix.
Picking several values from a short set: give each box its own `value` and bind them all to one array `v-model`.
A "select all" control over a partial selection: set `indeterminate` while only some children are checked.
avoidWhen: A form field that needs its own label, description, or helper text → wrap it in a horizontal `field` (`Field orientation="horizontal"` + `Field.Content`).
Each option needs a bordered card with a label and description → use a `field` choice card (`Field.Label` wrapping a horizontal `Field`).
An on/off setting that applies as soon as it flips → use `switch`.
Only one option of the set may be chosen → use `radio-button`.
related: field` — `orientation="horizontal"` puts the checkbox beside its label and description (the default inside forms); a `Field.Label` wrapping that Field turns it into a bordered choice card.
switch` — on/off toggle for settings that take effect immediately.
multi-select` — renders this checkbox in every option row; use it when the option list is long.
table` — uses this checkbox for row selection and the select-all header.
bestPractices: Set `binary` for a plain true/false value; without it the checkbox adds or removes its `value` in an array `modelValue`.
Give every checkbox an accessible name: point a `label` element's `for` at `inputId`, or pass `aria-label` (attributes land on the inner input).
indeterminate` only changes the visual and sets the native `indeterminate` property (exposed as mixed); the parent computes it and decides what a click does.
Use `readonly` for a value that cannot change in this context and `disabled` for an option that is unavailable.

props.name: modelValue
props.doc: Two-way bound value. Boolean in `binary` mode, scalar when paired with `value`, array when multi-selecting.

props.name: value
props.doc: Identifier for this checkbox in non-binary mode. Compared against `modelValue` (or included in the array).

props.name: binary
props.doc: When true, the checkbox toggles `modelValue` as a boolean (no `value` pairing).

props.name: indeterminate
props.doc: Renders the indeterminate visual (horizontal bar). Does not affect `modelValue`; the parent owns the tri-state logic.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables interaction and applies disabled tokens.

props.name: readonly
props.doc: Marks the field read-only; value is visible but cannot change via interaction.

props.name: inputId
props.doc: Forwarded to the inner `<input id>` for label association.

events.name: update:modelValue
events.notes: Fires on activation. Payload is the next boolean (binary mode) or the next array (every other mode).

examples.name: Default
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import Checkbox from '@aziontech/webkit/checkbox'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const checked = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <Checkbox
    v-model="checked"
    binary
    input-id="webkit-checkbox"
    aria-label="Toggle option"
  />
</template>
